body:
## Problem

`@adlc/opencode` does not load in OpenCode 2. With `opencode v2.0.20` installed, the server reports:

```
Server plugin error — @adlc/opencode
Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function.
```

The cause is the plugin API. `plugins/adlc-opencode/index.mjs` default-exports the v1 shape: an async function `adlcRailsGuard({ directory, worktree, project, client }, options)` that returns an object of string-keyed hooks (`tool.execute.before`, `event`, `permission.ask`, ...) plus a `tool` map built with `tool()` / `tool.schema` from `@opencode-ai/plugin` (zod). OpenCode 2 does not run v1 plugin implementations at all. It requires `export default Plugin.define({ id, setup(ctx) })` from the new package `@opencode/plugin` (npm latest 2.0.21), and every hook, tool and event subscription is registered through `ctx` inside `setup`.

While the plugin fails to load, no ADLC enforcement runs in OpenCode 2: no rails-guard deny, no build-gate backstop, no context injection, and no `adlc_gate` / `adlc_prosecute` tools.

References, which the implementer must read first:
- https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/ (config and overall migration)
- https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/migrate-v1 (plugin port: entrypoint, context, hook mapping table, tools, events, options)
- https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/plugins/ (full v2 plugin context API)

## Decisions (made with the human during P0)

1. **v2 only.** Remove the v1 implementation. Do not ship the dual `setup()` + `server()` export. Drop the `@opencode-ai/plugin` peer and dev dependency and the `opencode-ai@1.17.13` CI pin. The new peer dependency is `@opencode/plugin` at the v2 major (`>=2.0.20 <3`), still optional like the old one, plus a matching root devDependency so unit tests exercise the real package.
2. **Unmapped v1 hooks are ported to the closest v2 equivalent.** If no faithful equivalent exists, the hook is documented as a known v2 gap, and a test pins what happens instead. Details are below.
3. **The scaffold writes the native v2 config key.** `adlc-opencode` scaffold (`lib/scaffold.mjs` `ensurePluginRegistered`) writes `plugins` (not `plugin`) in `.opencode/opencode.json`, using the v2 entry shape (a string, or `{ "package": ..., "options": {...} }`). An existing v1 `plugin` array is migrated: our own entry, in any spelling `isOwnPluginEntry` recognises, moves to `plugins`, and other plugins' entries are preserved. Each moved entry is converted from a v1 tuple `[name, opts]` to `{ package, options }`. If `plugin` is empty afterwards, it is removed. If both keys exist, the result has exactly one ADLC entry. The existing fail-closed behaviour on an unparseable `opencode.json` stays.
4. **One ticket.** A half-ported entrypoint still fails to load, so the entrypoint, hooks, tools, tests, CI and docs land together.

## What to build

Rewrite `plugins/adlc-opencode/index.mjs` as `export default Plugin.define({ id: 'adlc', setup(ctx) { ... } })`, keeping the stable id `adlc`. Port every v1 extension point using the guide's mapping table:

| v1 (today) | v2 target |
| --- | --- |
| `directory` / `worktree` / `project` | `ctx.location.directory` / `ctx.location.project` (the repo root still prefers the worktree, as today) |
| `options` 2nd argument | `ctx.options` (still fed through `optionsToEnv`; env still wins; audited bypasses still NOT mappable) |
| `client.tui.showToast` / `client.app.log` in `makeNotify` | the v2 context equivalents (find them in the plugin context reference), with stderr as the always-available fallback; never throws |
| `tool.execute.before` (rails-guard, build-gate, handoff) | `ctx.tool.hook('execute.before', event => ...)`. Read `event.tool` and `event.input` (no separate output). A thrown error MUST still abort the tool call. |
| `tool.execute.after` (flail) | `ctx.tool.hook('execute.after', ...)` |
| `tool` map (`adlc_gate`, `adlc_prosecute`) | `ctx.tool.transform(editor => editor.add({ name, description, input: <JSON Schema>, execute }))`. Convert the zod args in `lib/gate-tool.mjs` / `lib/prosecute-tool.mjs` to JSON Schema, and return `{ content }`. The transform callback stays synchronous and side-effect free. |
| `tool.definition` (rail notice on edit/write/apply_patch) | `ctx.tool.transform(...)` updating those tools' descriptions |
| `event` (`session.compacted`, `file.edited`) | `ctx.event.subscribe({ signal })` loop, aborted by the cleanup function `setup` returns |
| `session.created` / `session.idle` hooks | handled from the same event subscription |
| `permission.ask` (dormant in v1) | `ctx.permission.hook('evaluate', ...)`. Check in the v2 source whether it is actually dispatched. If it is, it becomes a live deny lever and must be tested as one; update the "DORMANT" comment either way. |
| `experimental.chat.system.transform` | `ctx.session.hook('context', e => e.system.push({ type: 'text', text }))` |
| `experimental.session.compacting` | `ctx.session.hook('compaction', ...)` |
| `command.execute.before` (order and tamper advisories) | `ctx.session.hook('prompt', ...)`, detecting ADLC slash-commands from the prompt source/data. Advisory only; never blocks. |
| `experimental.compaction.autocontinue` (suppress auto-continue for degraded high-risk sessions) | No direct v2 hook. Rebuild it from the `compaction` hook plus the event stream if the v2 API lets the plugin stop or require a human turn after compaction. If it does not, document it as a known v2 gap in `docs/integrations/opencode.md`, and add a test asserting that after compaction a degraded high-risk session still gets the build-gate deny on its next structured mutation (the existing backstop). |

Keep the decision modules (`rails-checker.mjs`, `lib/build-gate.mjs`, `lib/handoff-gate.mjs`, `lib/watcher.mjs`, `lib/session-hooks.mjs`, `lib/context-inject.mjs`, `lib/compaction.mjs`, `lib/command-gate.mjs`, `lib/flail.mjs`) semantically unchanged. Only the adapter layer changes. Remove `@opencode-ai/plugin` references from them, such as JSDoc typedefs and comments citing v1.17.x contracts, or rewrite those references against v2.

Fail-open vs fail-closed directions MUST be preserved and asserted in tests:
- The rails-guard and build-gate deny ENFORCE by default (throw aborts the call). `ADLC_ALLOW_ADVISORY_HOOKS=1` or the option `advisoryHooks:true` is the only downgrade, and the context-handoff deny ignores it.
- Advisory hooks (flail, context injection, compaction context, command advisories, session audits, watcher) never throw into the host.
- If `@opencode/plugin` is missing, or tool registration fails, the native tools are not registered and a visible message says so. The rails hook still registers.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **The plugin loads in OpenCode 2.** In a temp project scaffolded with `node plugins/adlc-opencode/bin/cli.mjs` (the scaffold entry), run `opencode` v2 (>= 2.0.20). It lists the plugin with id `adlc` in its active plugin list and logs no `Server plugin error`. Verify with `opencode run` against the live-proof harness, below.
2. **Live deny proof on v2.** `node scripts/opencode-live-deny.mjs --require` passes against an opencode 2.x binary. The CONTROL run lands the write. In the TREATMENT run (`ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1`), the frozen rail file is unchanged and the tool result contains the rails-guard deny message. The script is ported to v2 config (`plugins` key) and the v2 server/headless contract.
3. **Live native-tool proof on v2.** `node scripts/opencode-live-tool.mjs --require` passes on opencode 2.x. The model can call `adlc_gate` and gets structured content back. `scripts/opencode-live-compaction.mjs` and `scripts/opencode-live-prosecute.mjs` are ported off `@opencode-ai/plugin` and pass.
4. **CI pins v2.** In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the pinned opencode live job installs a specific opencode 2.x version (no `opencode-ai@1.17.13` remains), and the `opencode-live-latest` drift canary tracks the v2 latest. Use the v2 install method the docs specify; if it is not npm `opencode-ai`, use the official installer pinned to a version. If PR #1168 has tiered CI definitions as a trust root by the time this builds, follow its ceremony for the workflow edit.
5. **Unit tests are ported.** Every test under `plugins/adlc-opencode/test/` that drives the plugin through the v1 shape (calling `adlcRailsGuard(...)` and invoking returned hooks by string key) instead drives the v2 default export. It calls `setup` with a fake `ctx` that records `ctx.tool.hook` / `ctx.tool.transform` / `ctx.session.hook` / `ctx.permission.hook` / `ctx.event.subscribe` registrations, then invokes those registrations. The fake ctx is built from the real `@opencode/plugin` types/package where it exposes one; a shape the real host never produces is a hollow mock, so check it against the v2 docs/source. `npm test -w plugins/adlc-opencode` (or `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/*.test.mjs`) passes.
6. **Scaffold writes v2 config.** New tests in `test/scaffold.test.mjs` cover four cases. (a) A fresh scaffold writes `plugins: [...]` with the ADLC entry and no `plugin` key. (b) An existing v1 `plugin` array holding our entry plus another plugin's tuple is migrated: ours moves to `plugins` as `{ package, options }` with its options preserved, the other entry is preserved, and an empty `plugin` key is removed. (c) Running it again is idempotent. (d) An unparseable `opencode.json` still fails closed and leaves the file untouched.
7. **No v1 API remains.** `rg -n "@opencode-ai/plugin|opencode-ai@1\.|tool\.schema" plugins/adlc-opencode scripts .github package.json` returns no matches. Leftovers in CHANGELOG history are fine.
8. **Docs updated.** `docs/integrations/opencode.md` and `plugins/adlc-opencode/README.md` state that OpenCode 2 is required, show the v2 `plugins` config, and list any known v2 gaps (at minimum the autocontinue outcome and the `permission.evaluate` status). ADR 0004 gets an addendum recording the v2-only decision. `apps/docs/lib/integration-facts.mjs` is updated so `scripts/test/docs-truth.test.mjs` passes. CHANGELOG notes the breaking change.
9. **All gates pass.** `npm run preflight` passes (tests, rail-freeze, mutation-gate) on the branch.

## Context

- Open PRs [#1154](https://github.com/voodootikigod/adlc/pull/1154) (opencode: fail closed on killed gates, fence prosecutor prompts, bound spawns) and [#1141](https://github.com/voodootikigod/adlc/pull/1141) (opencode: run each P5 lens on its own model) also edit `plugins/adlc-opencode/`. Rebase onto whichever has merged. If they are still open, coordinate rather than overwrite their behaviour; their logic lives mostly in `lib/` and should carry over unchanged.
- `lib/keyless-bridge.mjs` uses the v1 SDK (`client.session.create` / `client.session.prompt`, v1.17.13) for isolated child sessions. Port it to the v2 `ctx.session` domain or `@opencode/client`, per the server-API section of the migration guide.
- The plugin package is not a trust-root package (`packages/rails-guard`, `prosecute`, `gate-manifest`, `build-gate`), so a same-model P5 is sufficient. It still enforces rails, though, so the prosecutor must confirm the deny direction against the live v2 binary, not only mocks.
title: opencode plugin: port @adlc/opencode to the OpenCode v2 plugin API (Plugin.define + setup(ctx)) and drop v1
